findings.source_passage: Run over a few:—The Authors of the Bible; Aristotle; Pliny; Aldrovandi; Sir Thomas Browne; Gesner; Ray; Linnæus; Rondeletius; Willoughby; Green; Artedi; Sibbald; Brisson; Marten; Lacépède; Bonneterre; Desmarest; Baron Cuvier; Frederick Cuvier; John Hunter; Owen; Scoresby; Beale; Bennett; J. Ross Browne; the Author of Miriam Coffin; Olmstead; and the Rev. T. Cheever.
findings.why_it_matters: This cataloguing list is one of the chapter's most recognizable rhetorical gestures—its mock-scholarly sweep from Scripture to Rev. T. Cheever is a signature of Melville's encyclopedic irony and a critically noted set-piece. The draft collapses it to 'from the Authors of the Bible and Aristotle, down to Scoresby, Beale, and Bennett,' destroying the comic accumulation and voice entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full list verbatim, or at minimum retain enough names (including the eccentric 'Author of Miriam Coffin,' 'Rev. T. Cheever') to preserve the satiric sweep; the list itself is the joke.

findings.source_passage: this leviathan seems the banished and unconquerable Cain of his race, bearing for his mark that style upon his back
findings.source_locator: BOOK I, Chapter III, Fin-Back, near end
findings.why_it_matters: The Cain simile is one of the most interpretively charged passages in the chapter, linking the Fin-Back's solitude and mark to a biblical archetype of exile; the draft renders it as merely 'a Cain among whales,' stripping 'banished and unconquerable' and 'bearing for his mark,' which are the load-bearing words.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum 'the banished and unconquerable Cain of his race, bearing for his mark that style upon his back' to retain the interpretive and rhetorical weight.

findings.source_passage: as these pig-fish are a noisy, contemptible set, mostly lurking in the mouths of rivers, and feeding on wet hay, and especially as they do not spout, I deny their credentials as whales; and have presented them with their passports to quit the Kingdom of Cetology.
findings.source_locator: footnote to the grand divisions paragraph, Lamatins/Dugongs
findings.why_it_matters: This footnote is a prime specimen of Melville's mock-bureaucratic satirical voice—'feeding on wet hay,' 'presented them with their passports to quit the Kingdom of Cetology' are phrase-level signatures. The draft reduces it to the bare factual claim 'they do not spout,' erasing the comic register entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Dugong/Lamatin footnote with its key comic phrases: 'noisy, contemptible set,' 'feeding on wet hay,' 'presented them with their passports to quit the Kingdom of Cetology.'

findings.source_passage: If you yourself can withstand three cheers at beholding these vivacious fish, then heaven help ye; the spirit of godly gamesomeness is not in ye.
findings.source_locator: BOOK III, Chapter I, Huzza Porpoise
findings.why_it_matters: This aside is characteristic of Ishmael's rhetorical address to the reader—the mock-evangelical challenge is voice-defining and funny; its absence flattens the Huzza Porpoise entry into mere description.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the direct reader-address: 'If you yourself can withstand three cheers at beholding these vivacious fish, then heaven help ye; the spirit of godly gamesomeness is not in ye.'

summary: One high-severity loss (the full author-list enumeration collapsed to three names, destroying Melville's signature mock-encyclopedic irony) and three medium-severity voice flattenings (the Cain simile gutted, the Dugong footnote's comic bureaucratic register erased, the Huzza Porpoise reader-address absent) require regeneration.
